newsitem.title: USA: McCurry says more work to be done in Middle East.
newsitem.headline: McCurry says more work to be done in Middle East.

text.p: White House spokesman Mike McCurry said on Friday Ambassador Dennis Ross' trip to the Middle East was "constructive" but far more work remains to be done.
Ross headed for home on Friday without scoring a breakthrough in an emergency mission to salvage crumbling Israeli-PLO talks.

McCurry said President Bill Clinton "hears that Ambassador Ross had meetings that were constructive, that Ambassador Ross has characterised and described. And it's clear that much more work will need to be done and will be done."
He said Clinton would meet Ross on Monday and get his report.

After a two-day shuttle between Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat, who was in Tunis, Ross said he would report back to Clinton and Secretary of State Madeleine Albright.

"They will want to consider the report before deciding what are the most appropriate next steps that might be taken," he told reporters after meeting Netanyahu. "One thing that's clear as I leave is that it's essential to re-establish calm."

Israeli-PLO talks have been frozen since Netanyahu broke ground last week for a Jewish settlement on an Arab East Jerusalem hillside, unleashing Palestinian rage in daily West Bank unrest. Arabs view East Jerusalem, which Israel occupied in 1967 and annexed, as the capital of a future Palestinian state.
